findings.title: Password show/hide toggle is broken by forced type="password"
findings.body: The password field was switched to `PasswordField` but still passes `type="password"`. In packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx, `PasswordField` sets `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` after it, so the caller's `type="password"` always wins. The eye toggle on the password step therefore does nothing and the password can never be revealed. Remove the explicit `type` prop.

findings.title: Unrelated accessibility regression: password visibility toggle removed from tab order
findings.body: The `tabIndex={-1}` added to the show/hide password button is unrelated to backup codes. It makes the toggle unreachable by keyboard for every PasswordField in the app, a regression for keyboard and screen-reader users. It should be reverted or put in a separate PR.

findings.title: Backup code can be replayed by concurrent logins (read-modify-write race)
findings.body: The backup code is consumed by decrypting the list, nulling the entry, and writing the whole list back with a plain `prisma.user.update`. There is no transaction, row lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent login requests that submit the same valid code can both read the unused list, both pass the `indexOf` check, and both succeed. This defeats the single-use guarantee. Consuming the code should be atomic, for example by re-reading inside a transaction with a version check or using a conditional update on the stored value.

findings.title: Closing the dialog on the backup codes step loses the codes and leaves parent state stale
findings.body: 2FA is enabled server-side when the TOTP code is accepted, but `onEnable()` (which updates the parent switch) is only called from the "Close" button on the backup codes step. Closing via the X, Escape, or overlay (`onOpenChange`) skips it, so the settings page still shows 2FA as off until reload. The one-time backup codes are also shown with no warning or confirmation, so the user can lose them permanently with no way to regenerate them without disabling 2FA.

findings.title: Enable test leaves the backup codes dialog open and does not handle the new step
findings.body: The enable test now lands on the backup codes screen after entering the TOTP code, but it never clicks `backup-codes-close` and then asserts the switch state. The assertion at this line relies on a FIXME-noted weak check that passes even when the switch is unchecked, so the test does not verify the real end state. There is also no test for the backup code login path, which the PR's own TODO acknowledges. The PR checklist states no tests were added for the feature.

findings.title: Interactive button nested inside an anchor element
findings.body: The download control renders a `<Button>` inside `<a download href=...>`. Nesting interactive content inside a link is invalid HTML and gives inconsistent keyboard and screen-reader behavior (two focusable targets for one action). The anchor should carry the styling or the button should be the link.
